Keep Clincoo Env Variable Names Consistently Uppercase

API_URL and api_url are two different keys. Consistent uppercase spelling prevents silent undefined values.

This article is available in: Indonesia · English

POSIX environments treat variable names as case-sensitive. A .env file that mixes Api_Url and API_URL makes fetch use an empty string with no parse error.

Pick one style: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. Record that name in .env.example without secret values. Code and the deploy dashboard must copy the same spelling.

At boot, check required keys. If one is undefined, fail fast with the expected name. Do not continue with a silent localhost fallback in production.

Do not print secret values while debugging a misspelled name. Log only whether the key exists. A token printed in the Console or a CI log is already leaked.

Clincoo and the build script only see the strings you set. Clean spelling is cheaper than hunting a typo after release.
